af.name: Afghanistan
af.fact: A long, thin strip of mountains called the Wakhan Corridor stretches from its northeast corner all the way to a short border with China.

al.name: Albania
al.fact: Under dictator Enver Hoxha, more than 170,000 concrete bunkers were built across the country — you can still find them on beaches, in fields, and up in the mountains.

dz.name: Algeria
dz.fact: It's the largest country in Africa by area, and more than four-fifths of it is covered by the Sahara Desert.

ad.name: Andorra
ad.fact: This tiny country high in the Pyrenees has two heads of state at the same time: the President of France and the Bishop of Urgell in Spain, who share the title of co-prince.

ao.name: Angola
ao.fact: Its capital, Luanda, was founded by Portuguese settlers in 1576, and Portuguese is still the official language today.

ag.name: Antigua and Barbuda
ag.fact: Antigua is famous for having 365 beaches — locals like to say there's one for every day of the year.

ar.name: Argentina
ar.fact: Aconcagua, nearly 7,000 m (23,000 ft) tall, is the highest mountain anywhere outside Asia — and the tango dance grew up in the streets of Buenos Aires.

am.name: Armenia
am.fact: Around the year 301 CE it became the first country in the world to make Christianity its official religion.

au.name: Australia
au.fact: It's the only country that is also an entire continent, and the Great Barrier Reef off its northeast coast is the largest coral reef system on Earth.

at.name: Austria
at.fact: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg, and Vienna was home to famous composers like Haydn, Beethoven, and Schubert.

az.name: Azerbaijan
az.fact: It's nicknamed the 'Land of Fire' — at Yanar Dag near Baku, a hillside burns non-stop, fueled by natural gas seeping out of the ground.

bs.name: The Bahamas
bs.fact: In 1492 Christopher Columbus made his first landing in the Americas on one of these islands, which he named San Salvador.

bh.name: Bahrain
bh.fact: This island country in the Persian Gulf is connected to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway, a 25 km (15.5 mi) chain of bridges and causeways.

bd.name: Bangladesh
bd.fact: The Sundarbans, which it shares with India, is the largest mangrove forest in the world and a home of the Bengal tiger.

bb.name: Barbados
bb.fact: In 2021 it became a republic, replacing Queen Elizabeth II as head of state. It's also the home island of singer Rihanna.

by.name: Belarus
by.fact: The Białowieża Forest, shared with Poland, is one of the last pieces of the ancient forest that once covered Europe — and a home of the rare European bison.

be.name: Belgium
be.fact: Famous for chocolate and waffles, it's also where you'll find the headquarters of both the European Union and NATO, in Brussels.

bz.name: Belize
bz.fact: The Great Blue Hole, a giant round underwater sinkhole about 300 m (1,000 ft) across, sits within the second-largest barrier reef system in the world.

bj.name: Benin
bj.fact: This was once the home of the Kingdom of Dahomey, which was famous for its all-female army of warriors.

bt.name: Bhutan
bt.fact: Its government measures success with 'Gross National Happiness', and its huge forests soak up more carbon dioxide than the whole country produces.

bo.name: Bolivia
bo.fact: Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world. After it rains, it turns into a giant mirror that reflects the sky.

ba.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
ba.fact: The Stari Most ('Old Bridge') in Mostar was built in 1566, destroyed during a war in 1993, and rebuilt and reopened in 2004.

bw.name: Botswana
bw.fact: The Okavango Delta is a vast inland delta: the Okavango River never reaches the sea and instead spreads out into the Kalahari.

br.name: Brazil
br.fact: Most of the Amazon rainforest — the largest tropical rainforest on Earth — is here, and it's the only country in South America whose official language is Portuguese.

bn.name: Brunei
bn.fact: Kampong Ayer, a 'water village' of homes, schools, and mosques built on stilts over the Brunei River, has been nicknamed the 'Venice of the East'.

bg.name: Bulgaria
bg.fact: It's one of the world's top producers of rose oil, a precious perfume ingredient made from roses grown in its famous Rose Valley.

bf.name: Burkina Faso
bf.fact: Its name means 'land of upright (honest) people.' Until 1984 the country was called Upper Volta.

bi.name: Burundi
bi.fact: Lake Tanganyika, on its western border, is the longest freshwater lake in the world and the second deepest.

cv.name: Cabo Verde
cv.fact: These volcanic islands lie in the Atlantic off West Africa. Pico do Fogo, the highest peak, is an active volcano that last erupted in 2014.

kh.name: Cambodia
kh.fact: Angkor Wat, built in the 1100s, is the largest religious complex in the world — and it appears right on the national flag.

cm.name: Cameroon
cm.fact: It's nicknamed 'Africa in miniature' because it has a bit of everything: beaches, rainforests, mountains, savannas, and desert.

ca.name: Canada
ca.fact: It has the longest coastline of any country on Earth, and its border with the United States is the longest international land border in the world.

cf.name: Central African Republic
cf.fact: As its name suggests, it sits close to the center of Africa. It's landlocked, so it has no coastline at all.

td.name: Chad
td.fact: It's named after Lake Chad, a huge but shallow lake that shrank dramatically between the 1960s and the 1980s.

cl.name: Chile
cl.fact: It stretches more than 4,300 km (2,670 mi) from north to south but is only about 350 km (217 mi) wide at its widest. Its Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.

cn.name: China
cn.fact: The Great Wall was built and rebuilt over about 2,000 years and runs for thousands of kilometers — but despite the famous myth, you can't see it from space with your bare eyes.

co.name: Colombia
co.fact: It's the only country in South America with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

km.name: Comoros
km.fact: The coelacanth, a 'living fossil' fish once thought to have gone extinct millions of years ago, was found living in the waters around these islands.

cg.name: Republic of the Congo
cg.fact: Its capital, Brazzaville, faces Kinshasa (the capital of its neighbor) across the Congo River — together they are the closest pair of capital cities in the world.

cr.name: Costa Rica
cr.fact: It abolished its army in 1948, and about a quarter of its land is protected in national parks and reserves.

ci.name: Côte d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast)
ci.fact: It is the world's largest producer of cocoa beans, the main ingredient in chocolate.

hr.name: Croatia
hr.fact: More than 1,000 islands and islets dot its Adriatic coast, and the Dalmatian dog breed is named after its Dalmatia region.

cu.name: Cuba
cu.fact: It's the largest island in the Caribbean, and the bee hummingbird — the world's smallest bird — lives only here.

cy.name: Cyprus
cy.fact: According to Greek mythology, the goddess Aphrodite was born from the sea foam off this island's coast.

cz.name: Czechia
cz.fact: According to Guinness World Records, Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle in the world — and Prague's astronomical clock has been ticking since 1410.

cd.name: DR Congo
cd.fact: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, with measured depths of more than 220 m (720 ft).

dk.name: Denmark
dk.fact: LEGO was invented here. The name comes from the Danish words 'leg godt', which mean 'play well'.

dj.name: Djibouti
dj.fact: Lake Assal lies about 155 m (509 ft) below sea level, making it the lowest point in all of Africa.

dm.name: Dominica
dm.fact: Nicknamed the 'Nature Isle of the Caribbean', it has a Boiling Lake — a flooded volcanic vent where the water bubbles and steams.

do.name: Dominican Republic
do.fact: Santo Domingo, founded in 1496, is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas.

ec.name: Ecuador
ec.fact: It's named after the Equator, which runs right through it. Its Galápagos Islands helped inspire Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.

eg.name: Egypt
eg.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World that is still standing.

sv.name: El Salvador
sv.fact: It's the smallest country in Central America and is nicknamed the 'Land of Volcanoes' because it has more than 20 of them.

gq.name: Equatorial Guinea
gq.fact: It's the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.

er.name: Eritrea
er.fact: Its capital, Asmara, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site full of 1930s modernist buildings — including the Fiat Tagliero, a gas station shaped like an airplane.

ee.name: Estonia
ee.fact: Skype was created by engineers here, and it's one of the most digital countries on Earth, with almost all government services available online.

sz.name: Eswatini
sz.fact: It's one of the world's last absolute monarchies, and in 2018 it changed its name from Swaziland.

et.name: Ethiopia
et.fact: Coffee is believed to have first come from this region, and the country uses its own calendar that has 13 months.

fj.name: Fiji
fj.fact: It's made up of more than 330 islands, and the 180° line of longitude — exactly opposite the Prime Meridian — passes right through it.

fi.name: Finland
fi.fact: It's nicknamed the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes', but it actually has more than 180,000 of them.

fr.name: France
fr.fact: It's the most visited country in the world. The Eiffel Tower, built for the 1889 World's Fair, was only given a permit to stand for 20 years.

ga.name: Gabon
ga.fact: Rainforest covers most of the country, and in 2002 it created 13 national parks at once, protecting about a tenth of its land.

gm.name: The Gambia
gm.fact: It's the smallest country on mainland Africa — a thin strip of land along the Gambia River, surrounded by Senegal except for its short coast.

ge.name: Georgia
ge.fact: Archaeologists have found evidence that people were making wine here about 8,000 years ago — among the oldest winemaking on Earth.

de.name: Germany
de.fact: Around 1440, Johannes Gutenberg developed his printing press in Mainz, which changed how books — and ideas — spread around the world.

gh.name: Ghana
gh.fact: In 1957 it became the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence. Before that it was called the Gold Coast.

gr.name: Greece
gr.fact: The ancient Olympic Games began at Olympia in 776 BCE, and the first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.

gd.name: Grenada
gd.fact: Nicknamed the 'Spice Isle', it's a major producer of nutmeg — which even appears on its flag.

gt.name: Guatemala
gt.fact: Tikal, hidden in the northern rainforest, was one of the greatest cities of the ancient Maya, with temples rising above the treetops.

gn.name: Guinea
gn.fact: It's called the 'water tower of West Africa' because the Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers all begin in its highlands.

gw.name: Guinea-Bissau
gw.fact: Cashew nuts make up most of its exports, and the Bijagós islands off its coast are a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

gy.name: Guyana
gy.fact: It's the only country in South America where English is the official language, and Kaieteur Falls drops about 226 m (741 ft) in a single plunge.

ht.name: Haiti
ht.fact: In 1804 it became the first independent nation in Latin America and the first country born from a successful revolt by enslaved people.

hn.name: Honduras
hn.fact: The ancient Maya city of Copán is famous for its Hieroglyphic Stairway, carved with the longest known Maya inscription.

hu.name: Hungary
hu.fact: Budapest sits on more than 100 natural hot springs, and the Rubik's Cube was invented here by Ernő Rubik in 1974.

is.name: Iceland
is.fact: It sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two tectonic plates are slowly pulling apart, and it has around 30 active volcanic systems.

in.name: India
in.fact: In 2023 it passed China to become the world's most populous country. The Taj Mahal in Agra is one of the most famous buildings on Earth.

id.name: Indonesia
id.capital: Jakarta (a new capital, Nusantara, is being built)
id.fact: It's the world's largest island country, with more than 17,000 islands, and it's home to the Komodo dragon — the biggest lizard on Earth.

ir.name: Iran
ir.fact: Once known as Persia, it was the center of one of the world's first great empires, founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BCE.

iq.name: Iraq
iq.fact: Ancient Mesopotamia, the 'land between the rivers' Tigris and Euphrates, was here — and it's where some of the world's earliest writing, called cuneiform, was invented.

ie.name: Ireland
ie.fact: Halloween traces its roots to Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival that marked the end of the harvest and the start of winter.

il.name: Israel
il.fact: The Dead Sea, on its border with Jordan, is the lowest place on land — more than 400 m (1,300 ft) below sea level — and so salty that you float.

it.name: Italy
it.fact: Two whole countries — Vatican City and San Marino — sit inside its borders, and the city of Venice is built on 118 small islands linked by canals and bridges.

jm.name: Jamaica
jm.fact: It's the birthplace of reggae music and Bob Marley — and of Usain Bolt, who holds the 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds.

jp.name: Japan
jp.fact: It's made up of thousands of islands, and its tallest mountain, Mount Fuji, is a volcano that rises 3,776 m (12,388 ft).

jo.name: Jordan
jo.fact: Petra, an ancient city carved right into rose-red sandstone cliffs, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

kz.name: Kazakhstan
kz.fact: It's the largest landlocked country in the world, and the first human spaceflight, Yuri Gagarin's in 1961, launched from Baikonur here.

ke.name: Kenya
ke.fact: Every year more than a million wildebeest cross from Tanzania's Serengeti into the Maasai Mara during the Great Migration.

ki.name: Kiribati
ki.fact: It's the only country with islands in all four hemispheres — north, south, east, and west.

kw.name: Kuwait
kw.fact: Its money, the Kuwaiti dinar, is the highest-valued currency unit in the world.

kg.name: Kyrgyzstan
kg.fact: It lies in the Tian Shan and Pamir mountain ranges, and Lake Issyk-Kul, high in the mountains, rarely freezes even in winter because its water is slightly salty.

la.name: Laos
la.fact: It's the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, and its Plain of Jars is scattered with thousands of mysterious ancient stone jars.

lv.name: Latvia
lv.fact: Its capital, Riga, is famous for having one of the largest collections of Art Nouveau buildings in the world.

lb.name: Lebanon
lb.fact: The cedar tree on its flag has been a symbol here for thousands of years, and the ancient Phoenicians from this coast created an alphabet that inspired ours.

ls.name: Lesotho
ls.fact: It's completely surrounded by South Africa, and it's the only independent country that lies entirely above 1,000 m (3,281 ft).

lr.name: Liberia
lr.fact: In 1847 it became Africa's first independent republic. Its capital, Monrovia, is named after US President James Monroe.

ly.name: Libya
ly.fact: The Great Man-Made River is a giant network of underground pipes that carries ancient 'fossil' water from deep beneath the desert to its cities — the world's largest irrigation project.

li.name: Liechtenstein
li.fact: It's one of only two 'doubly landlocked' countries (surrounded only by landlocked countries), and it got rid of its army back in 1868.

lt.name: Lithuania
lt.fact: In 1989, a French scientist calculated that the geographic center of Europe lies just north of its capital, Vilnius.

lu.name: Luxembourg
lu.fact: It's the world's only remaining grand duchy — a country ruled by a grand duke — and one of the richest countries on Earth.

mg.name: Madagascar
mg.fact: It's the fourth-largest island on Earth, and lemurs — found in the wild almost nowhere else — live in its forests.

mw.name: Malawi
mw.fact: Lake Malawi has more species of fish than any other lake in the world, including at least 700 kinds of colorful cichlids.

my.name: Malaysia
my.fact: The Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.

mv.name: Maldives
mv.fact: It's the lowest-lying country on Earth: its highest natural point is only about 2.4 m (8 ft) above sea level.

ml.name: Mali
ml.fact: The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick building in the world, and Timbuktu was once a great center of trade and learning.

mt.name: Malta
mt.fact: Its Ġgantija temples were built more than 5,000 years ago — they're older than the pyramids of Egypt.

mh.name: Marshall Islands
mh.fact: The bikini swimsuit was named after Bikini Atoll here, days after the United States began testing nuclear bombs there in 1946.

mr.name: Mauritania
mr.fact: The Richat Structure — a giant ring of rock about 40 km (25 mi) wide in the Sahara, nicknamed the 'Eye of the Sahara' — is easy to spot from space.

mu.name: Mauritius
mu.fact: This island was the only known home of the dodo, a flightless bird that went extinct soon after people arrived in the 1600s.

mx.name: Mexico
mx.fact: Mexico City is built on top of the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the capital of the Aztec Empire.

fm.name: Micronesia
fm.fact: On the island of Pohnpei lie the ruins of Nan Madol, an ancient stone city built on nearly 100 artificial islets.

md.name: Moldova
md.fact: The Mileștii Mici winery holds a Guinness World Record for the largest wine collection — about 2 million bottles stored in huge underground tunnels.

mc.name: Monaco
mc.fact: It's the second-smallest country in the world (after Vatican City), and the famous Monaco Grand Prix Formula One race zooms through its streets.

mn.name: Mongolia
mn.fact: It's the most sparsely populated country in the world. Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire here in 1206 — the largest connected land empire in history.

me.name: Montenegro
me.fact: The Tara River Canyon, up to 1,300 m (4,300 ft) deep, is the deepest canyon in continental Europe.

ma.name: Morocco
ma.fact: UNESCO and Guinness World Records call the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859, the oldest continuously operating university in the world.

mz.name: Mozambique
mz.fact: Its flag is the only national flag in the world that shows a modern firearm (an AK-47 rifle), crossed with a hoe on top of an open book.

mm.name: Myanmar
mm.fact: The ancient city of Bagan still has the remains of more than 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas spread across its plains.

na.name: Namibia
na.fact: The Namib is thought to be the oldest desert on Earth, and its red sand dunes are some of the tallest in the world.

nr.name: Nauru
nr.fact: At just 21 km² (8 sq mi), it's the third-smallest country in the world — and it doesn't have an official capital city.

np.name: Nepal
np.fact: Eight of the world's 10 highest mountains are here, including Mount Everest (8,849 m / 29,032 ft). Its flag is the only national flag that isn't a rectangle.

nl.name: Netherlands
nl.capital: Amsterdam (The Hague is the seat of government)
nl.fact: About a quarter of the country (26%) lies below sea level, protected by dikes, dunes, and pumps — which were once powered by windmills.

nz.name: New Zealand
nz.fact: In 1893 it became the first self-governing country to give women the right to vote. Its only native land mammals are bats.

ni.name: Nicaragua
ni.fact: Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America, and even though it's freshwater, sharks swim in it.

ne.name: Niger
ne.fact: About four-fifths of the country lies in the Sahara, making it one of the hottest countries in the world.

ng.name: Nigeria
ng.fact: It has the most people of any country in Africa, and its huge movie industry is nicknamed 'Nollywood'.

kp.name: North Korea
kp.fact: Korea has been divided since 1945, and a 4 km (2.5 mi) wide Demilitarized Zone, or DMZ, separates North and South.

mk.name: North Macedonia
mk.fact: Lake Ohrid, which it shares with Albania, is one of Europe's deepest and oldest lakes, with more than 200 species found nowhere else.

no.name: Norway
no.fact: Its coastline is carved by more than 1,000 fjords, and the Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded in Oslo since 1901.

om.name: Oman
om.fact: Frankincense, a sweet-smelling tree resin, has been harvested and traded from here for thousands of years.

pk.name: Pakistan
pk.fact: K2, the second-highest mountain in the world at 8,611 m (28,251 ft), is on its border with China.

pw.name: Palau
pw.fact: In 2009 it created the world's first shark sanctuary, banning commercial shark fishing in its waters.

pa.name: Panama
pa.fact: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, lets ships cross between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans without sailing all the way around South America.

pg.name: Papua New Guinea
pg.fact: About 840 languages are spoken here, making it the most linguistically diverse country on Earth.

py.name: Paraguay
py.fact: The Itaipú Dam on the Paraná River, which it shares with Brazil, is one of the largest hydroelectric power plants in the world.

pe.name: Peru
pe.fact: Machu Picchu, a 15th-century Inca city high in the Andes, was built with stones cut so precisely that they fit together without mortar.

ph.name: Philippines
ph.fact: It's made up of about 7,641 islands, and colorful 'jeepneys' — first made from US military jeeps left over from World War II — are a famous way to get around.

pl.name: Poland
pl.fact: Marie Curie — the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the only person ever to win Nobels in two different sciences — was born in Warsaw.

pt.name: Portugal
pt.fact: Its sailors led the Age of Discovery. In 1498, Vasco da Gama became the first European to reach India by sea.

qa.name: Qatar
qa.fact: In 2022 it hosted the first FIFA World Cup ever held in the Middle East.

ro.name: Romania
ro.fact: Bran Castle, perched on a cliff in Transylvania, is famous for its link to the legend of Dracula.

ru.name: Russia
ru.fact: It's the largest country in the world, stretching across 11 time zones, and Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake on Earth.

rw.name: Rwanda
rw.fact: Known as the 'land of a thousand hills', it's one of the few places on Earth where you can see endangered mountain gorillas in the wild.

kn.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
kn.fact: It's the smallest country in the Western Hemisphere, both in land area and in population.

lc.name: Saint Lucia
lc.fact: The Pitons — two steep volcanic peaks rising straight out of the sea — are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the triangles on the flag represent them.

vc.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
vc.fact: La Soufrière, the volcano on the main island of Saint Vincent, erupted explosively in April 2021.

ws.name: Samoa
ws.fact: At the end of 2011 it jumped across the International Date Line and skipped December 30 completely.

sm.name: San Marino
sm.fact: According to tradition it was founded in 301 CE, and it claims to be the oldest surviving republic in the world.

st.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
st.fact: These volcanic islands sit almost exactly on the Equator in the Gulf of Guinea, and together they form Africa's second-smallest country.

sa.name: Saudi Arabia
sa.fact: The Rub' al Khali, or 'Empty Quarter', is the largest continuous sand desert in the world.

sn.name: Senegal
sn.fact: Its capital, Dakar, sits on the Cap-Vert peninsula — the westernmost point of mainland Africa.

rs.name: Serbia
rs.fact: Belgrade, one of the oldest cities in Europe, sits where the Sava River flows into the Danube.

sc.name: Seychelles
sc.fact: It's the smallest country in Africa, and the coco de mer palm that grows here has the largest seed of any plant on Earth.

sl.name: Sierra Leone
sl.fact: Its capital, Freetown, was founded in 1792 as a settlement for formerly enslaved people.

sg.name: Singapore
sg.fact: It's one of the world's few city-states — a whole country that is basically one city — and its symbol is the Merlion, half lion and half fish.

sk.name: Slovakia
sk.fact: Its capital, Bratislava, is the only national capital in the world that borders two other countries: Austria and Hungary.

si.name: Slovenia
si.fact: More than half the country is forest, and its caves are home to the olm — a blind, pale salamander that can live for more than 100 years.

sb.name: Solomon Islands
sb.fact: The island of Guadalcanal was the site of one of the biggest battles of World War II in the Pacific, in 1942–43.

so.name: Somalia
so.fact: It has the longest coastline of any country on mainland Africa, along the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

za.name: South Africa
za.fact: Nelson Mandela, who spent 27 years in prison for fighting racial injustice, became its first Black president in 1994.

kr.name: South Korea
kr.fact: The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was created in 1443 under King Sejong the Great so that ordinary people could learn to read and write.

ss.name: South Sudan
ss.fact: It's the world's newest country — it became independent in 2011.

es.name: Spain
es.fact: Construction of La Sagrada Família, the famous basilica designed by Antoni Gaudí in Barcelona, began in 1882 — and was still going more than 140 years later.

lk.name: Sri Lanka
lk.fact: It's one of the world's biggest tea exporters. 'Ceylon tea' is named after the island's old name, Ceylon.

sd.name: Sudan
sd.fact: Ancient Nubian kings built about 255 pyramids in this region — more than twice as many as ancient Egypt — at places like Meroë.

sr.name: Suriname
sr.fact: It's the smallest country in South America, and more than 90% of it is covered by rainforest.

se.name: Sweden
se.fact: Every winter, the Icehotel in the far-north village of Jukkasjärvi is built from blocks of snow and ice taken from the nearby Torne River.

ch.name: Switzerland
ch.fact: It has four national languages — German, French, Italian, and Romansh — and it has stayed neutral in wars since 1815.

sy.name: Syria
sy.fact: Its capital, Damascus, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

tj.name: Tajikistan
tj.fact: More than 90% of the country is mountains, including much of the Pamirs — nicknamed the 'Roof of the World'.

tz.name: Tanzania
tz.fact: Mount Kilimanjaro, at 5,895 m (19,341 ft), is the highest mountain in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain on Earth.

th.name: Thailand
th.fact: It's the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonized by a European power.

tl.name: Timor-Leste
tl.fact: When it gained independence in 2002, it became the first new sovereign country of the 21st century.

tg.name: Togo
tg.fact: It's one of the narrowest countries in Africa: a thin strip of land that stretches north for hundreds of kilometers from a short coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.

to.name: Tonga
to.fact: It's still a kingdom today, and it's the only Pacific island nation that never gave up its independence to a foreign power.

tt.name: Trinidad and Tobago
tt.fact: The steelpan drum was invented here, and Pitch Lake is the largest natural deposit of asphalt (bitumen) in the world.

tn.name: Tunisia
tn.fact: The ruins of ancient Carthage, Rome's great rival, are near the capital, and desert scenes for Star Wars were filmed here.

tr.name: Türkiye (Turkey)
tr.fact: Istanbul is the only major city in the world that sits on two continents — Europe and Asia — on either side of the Bosporus strait.

tm.name: Turkmenistan
tm.fact: The Darvaza gas crater, nicknamed the 'Door to Hell', is a giant pit in the desert that has been on fire since 1971.

tv.name: Tuvalu
tv.fact: It earns money by leasing out its internet domain, '.tv'. Its highest point is just 4.6 m (15 ft) above sea level.

ug.name: Uganda
ug.fact: It shares Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, with Kenya and Tanzania — and the White Nile flows north out of the lake near the town of Jinja.

ua.name: Ukraine
ua.fact: It's the largest country that lies entirely in Europe, and its rich black soil has earned it the nickname 'breadbasket of Europe'.

ae.name: United Arab Emirates
ae.fact: Dubai's Burj Khalifa, about 828 m (2,717 ft) tall, has been the tallest building in the world since it opened in 2010.

gb.name: United Kingdom
gb.fact: It's made up of four countries — England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. 'Big Ben' is actually the name of the giant bell, not the clock tower.

us.name: United States
us.fact: In 1872 it created Yellowstone, the world's first national park, and in 1969 its Apollo 11 mission landed the first humans on the Moon.

uy.name: Uruguay
uy.fact: It hosted — and won — the very first FIFA World Cup, in 1930.

uz.name: Uzbekistan
uz.fact: It's one of only two 'doubly landlocked' countries, and its ancient Silk Road cities, like Samarkand and Bukhara, are covered in shimmering blue tiles.

vu.name: Vanuatu
vu.fact: On Pentecost Island, men 'land dive' from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles — a tradition that inspired bungee jumping.

ve.name: Venezuela
ve.fact: Angel Falls is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world, plunging 979 m (3,212 ft).

vn.name: Vietnam
vn.fact: Hang Sơn Đoòng is the largest natural cave in the world. It has its own fast-flowing underground river and a bigger cross-section than any other known cave.

ye.name: Yemen
ye.fact: The old walled city of Shibam is packed with mud-brick tower houses, earning it the nickname 'Manhattan of the Desert'.

zm.name: Zambia
zm.fact: Victoria Falls, on the border with Zimbabwe, is known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya — 'the smoke that thunders'.

zw.name: Zimbabwe
zw.fact: The country is named after Great Zimbabwe, a medieval stone city whose huge walls were built without any mortar.
